title: t5: qualify Headscale 0.29.5 package and gate catalog publication
body:
## Summary

Qualifies the Headscale package on a live Cloudron and makes it ready for the
first catalog publication (task t5).

- Headscale 0.29.4 → **0.29.5**; the binary is checked against upstream
  `checksums.txt` (`e979d27f…be980`). `start.sh` now reads `HEADSCALE_VERSION`
  from the image instead of a hard-coded copy.
- STUN default **3479 → 3480**: Cloudron TURN uses 3478 and the NetBird
  package's optional STUN port defaults to 3479.
- Store listing: `DESCRIPTION.md`, `POSTINSTALL.md` (SSO and non-SSO variants),
  store-format `CHANGELOG`, square upstream icon, four slides rendered from
  `media/src/slide.html`, upstream licence, commit-pinned `iconUrl`/`mediaLinks`.
- Publication is now **gated** like opendesk: PRs and ungated `main` runs only
  validate (package test, ShellCheck, real Cloudron CLI 8.2.6 catalog dry run).
  Publication needs `CLOUDRON_PUBLICATION_ENABLED=true`, then builds and
  attests the image, generates and attests the catalog, commits it with the
  tag atomically, and creates the release. Previously every `main` push pushed
  an image.
- README and docs describe enrolment, management, relays, backups, and the
  qualification checklist.

**Merge with a merge commit, not squash**: `iconUrl` and `mediaLinks` are pinned
to `b0613489`, which must stay on `main`.

## Qualification evidence

Test install `headscale-test` on the maintainer's Cloudron (9.1, built on the
server from this branch). Disposable clients were `tailscale/tailscale:stable`
1.104.1 in Docker.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Local image build, start, `/health` | `{"status":"pass"}`, `version=v0.29.5`, `stun server started at [::]:3480` |
| STUN port disabled | Starts without embedded DERP; `/health` passes |
| Cloudron install and health | Installed, running, HTTPS `/health` 200 |
| `headscale users create`, `preauthkeys create` | OK |
| Two clients register with a pre-auth key | Both `Running`; server lists both online |
| Direct path | `pong … via 192.168.215.6:… in 0s` |
| Embedded DERP relay only (`TS_DEBUG_ALWAYS_USE_DERP`, `derp.urls: []`) | `pong … via DERP(headscale) in 75ms` |
| DERP over HTTPS 443 and STUN | `Successfully established a DERP connection`, IPv4 STUN response |
| SSO redirect | `/register/<id>` → 302 to Cloudron `/openid/auth`, `redirect_uri=…/oidc/callback` |
| Restart | Noise and DERP key hashes and users unchanged |
| Backup → add user → restore | Added user gone, keys unchanged, clients re-register |
| `cloudron update` to this commit | Keys, users unchanged; clients direct and via DERP |
| End-to-end Cloudron SSO (maintainer in browser) | "Node registered as Marcus Quinn"; node online at 100.64.0.3, user `marcus` with `provider: oidc` |

Headscale replaces a waiting device's sign-in link every 15 minutes (server
held `/machine/register` for 899.7 s, then issued a follow-up auth ID); opening
a stale link shows "Gone: Your session has expired". The README now says so.

The `tcp6 … network is unreachable` line in `tailscale debug derp` comes from
Docker Desktop having no IPv6, not the server.

## Remaining before publication

- Set `CLOUDRON_PUBLICATION_ENABLED=true` and merge with a merge commit. The
  GHCR package already exists and is anonymously pullable, then verify catalog
  and release.
- Community Apps listing and upstream monitoring follow publication.

## Verification

```sh
bash test/package-test.sh
shellcheck -x start.sh scripts/*.sh test/*.sh
```

Resolves #2

<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->
<!-- aidevops:sig -->
---
[aidevops.sh](https://aidevops.sh) v3.39.45 plugin for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) v1.19.3 with claude-opus-5-5 spent 9h 27m and 831,623 tokens on this with the user in an interactive session.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Headscale 0.29.5 adds Cloudron sign-in for connecting devices, pre-auth keys for servers and headless devices, and an embedded relay with STUN on UDP port 3480 by default.
  * Backups include the database, keys, and configuration; app data is preserved across version changes.
  * Updated store listing assets and expanded installation, device management, configuration, and backup guidance.

* **Improvements**
  * Cloudron package publication now uses gated catalog and release checks, with verification before publishing.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: fix: validate attested catalog contents before push (GH#22)
body:
## Summary

Resolves #22.

- Validate the attested catalog in the write-capable `push` job before copying it into the checkout.
- Require unchanged existing versions and top-level metadata, exactly the expected new version, published state, and the exact build-produced GHCR digest reference.
- Pass the build output directly through `push.needs` and add push-job-specific static regression checks in `test/package-test.sh`.

## Runtime Testing

- `bash test/package-test.sh`: passed.
- `shellcheck -x start.sh scripts/create-github-release.sh scripts/publish-cloudron-catalog.sh scripts/render-store-media.sh test/package-test.sh`: passed (explicit expansion of the issue's shell globs).
- `actionlint .github/workflows/cloudron-catalog-publish.yml`: passed.

- Direct behavioral validation of the workflow's exact jq program at `c340e5683c6c88a660a546561500ed372e2492d0`: accepted a valid publication and rejected 20 invalid catalogs (modified/removed history, extra/missing/wrong version, changed metadata, incorrect state/version/image, missing manifest, null/array catalogs, multiple/empty/malformed JSON, mutable tag, wrong repository, short/uppercase digest).

## Acceptance self-review

- Existing version objects and top-level metadata remain equal to the immutable source checkout.
- The candidate contains exactly the source version keys plus the expected new version; reusing an existing key is refused.
- New entry state, manifest version and image are checked against trusted job outputs; the image must be a lowercase SHA-256 digest in the intended repository.
- Validation runs after attestation verification and before copying or committing; `set -euo pipefail` stops on jq refusal.
- PR preflight and linked-issue CI passed. No real publication was triggered; next-version publication remains an explicit unverified integration criterion.

## Scope and limitations

Only `.github/workflows/cloudron-catalog-publish.yml` and `test/package-test.sh` change. Reference pattern: existing immutable-source and attestation verification immediately preceding the catalog copy. No permissions or publication authorization changes. No release is triggered: the next authorized real publication remains the end-to-end confirmation.

Sibling repository discovery found no matching catalog-attestation issue. Creating a sibling issue is outside this worker's assigned repository/issue write authority; the requested sibling follow-up remains to be routed by the owning session.

title: chore: resync framework workflow to aidevops canonical caller
body:
## Summary

Resync `.github/workflows/loc-badge.yml` to the canonical aidevops caller template
(reusable-workflow pattern, GH#20649 + GH#20727).

**Classification before**: `DRIFTED/CALLER`
**Ref**: `@main`

## Why

The aidevops framework ships managed GitHub Actions workflows as reusable
workflows. Downstream repos carry ~45-line callers that delegate all logic
to the configured aidevops reusable workflow repository/ref.

This PR brings this repo in line with the canonical template, eliminating
drift and unblocking automatic updates when the framework evolves.

## How to verify

After merge, trigger an event matching the workflow triggers. Framework
scripts are fetched at runtime via a secondary checkout — no
`.agents/scripts/` files are needed in this repo.

## Rollback

If the workflow breaks, revert this PR. The previous workflow is preserved
in git history at the parent commit.

Generated by: `aidevops sync-workflows --apply` (see marcusquinn/aidevops#20649).
